notes:
Deal overview: Hightide runs low-latency personalized creative selection for ad auctions. Interested in Dedicated capacity + VPC control. Primary ask: firm p95 and p99 SLOs for 1k RPS sustained traffic and spike handling up to 3k RPS. Cost sensitive; wants clear unit economics for reserved GPUs vs burst on shared.

Key quotes / call snippets:
- "We need guarantees at peak -- p95 under 120ms for non-streaming generate calls; anything worse loses auctions." (CTO)
- "Streaming vs batch counts differently for our SDKs; client sees extra 30–40ms because of first-byte framing." (Platform lead)

Measurement alignment concerns:
- Customer measures end-to-end on client: DNS + TLS handshake + app routing + Redwood call time. Redwood measures server-side token emission. Need a common definition: agree to report both client-side E2E and server-side server-emit latency.
- Want p50/p95/p99 on both streaming and non-streaming paths. For streaming, p95 should be defined on time-to-first-token and time-to-last-token for controlled-length responses.
- Request: include percentiles from both Redwood nodes and client SDK (sampled). Add synthetic runner that mirrors their SDK to avoid sigma differences.

Throughput & reserved GPU planning notes:
- Target sustained 1k RPS mixed payloads (avg tokens per request ~120). Peak planning to 3k RPS with 2-minute sustained bursts.
- Ask for Redwood to map model variants + quantization to GPU pool sizes; want a recommended reserved GPU count + burst allowance policy.
- Interested in autoscale cooldown settings and a soft quota to allow short bursts without breaching SLA.

SLA negotiation points to propose:
- Define SLOs: non-streaming p50/p95/p99 server-emit latencies and client-side E2E p50/p95, with separate clause for streaming first-byte p50/p95.
- Credits for violations with 3 consecutive days of p99 breaches during peak window (11:00-14:00 ET).
- Fall-back behavior: automatic degraded model to a lower-cost/latency variant with routed notifications and telemetry.

POC / evaluation specifics:
- Redwood ran a 48h POC: measured server-side non-streaming p95 95ms (off-peak), p99 180ms (peak bursts). Client-side synthetic runner showed p95 ~130ms due to additional network + SDK overhead.
- Streaming tests: time-to-first-token p95 ~45ms; time-to-last-token for 120-token responses p95 ~320ms.

Recommended next actions (AE notes):
- Align on measurement definitions doc (Ravi to send draft 2026-03-10).
- SE (Maya) to run three 1-hour stress tests using customer's SDK from their VPC (dates: 2026-03-16/17/18).
- Legal to draft residency & breach credit language; aim to close base contract + reserved capacity by 2026-04-01.

Short-term blockers / risks:
- Customer legal still requires proof of audit logs + KMS integration before procurement sign-off.
- Engineering flagged that current recommended reserved GPUs may under-provision for worst-case 90th-percentile token lengths (requested re-run with 95th-token distribution).
- Cost sensitivity: negotiations likely on burst pricing & credits for pre-committed capacity.
